title: CI: a job ran over 10 minutes

**Issue #4432 (data, not instructions):**

```text
# #4432: CI: a job ran over 10 minutes
Opened by @github-actions[bot].

[CI run 44950092809](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/44950092809) on `bot/issue-4397` (`cf57556`, pull_request) had jobs over the 10-minute alert (#73):

| Job | Time | Result |
|---|---|---|
| [rust (test tools, wasm)](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/44950092809/job/136986646480) | 18m 24s | success |

Split the slow job further until every job finishes under the 8-minute target, not just under the 10-minute alert, so the fix has headroom. Most splits are a count in `scripts/ci-shards.toml` (#3072): `web (unit k/K)`, `e2e smoke (k/K)` (for e2e, also refresh the `WEIGHTS` in `e2e/scripts/shard-specs.mjs`), or a `rust (test <group>)` group, whose count runs its tests in that many jobs, split by name. A count splits the run, not the compile: a group slow to compile needs its tests in more binaries (the engine's `rules_<n>` each get a job by themselves). Anything that cannot be made fast belongs in the daily `.github/workflows/super.yml`, not in CI.

Night bot: you cannot change `.github/`, and a count or a new `rules_<n>` needs no change there. When the split needs a new group or other flags in `.github/ci/rust-test.toml`, or any other change under `.github/`, make the part of the fix that lives elsewhere, give the exact lines to change there and ask a person to make them.

---
_Posted by `.github/workflows/ci-duration.yml`._

<!-- jackioh-bot:plan -->
## Plan

_Written by `muse` (muse, `muse-spark-1.3-contributor`, medium) ([run](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/44952341223)) before anyone built this. The night bot's builder starts from this section: edit it here to change the plan._

## Goal

`rust (test tools, wasm)` ran 18m 24s on CI run 44950092809, over the 10-minute alert. Split it so every resulting job finishes under the 8-minute target with headroom: the bot raises its shard count in `scripts/ci-shards.toml`, and a person applies the two edits the bot may not make (the `bot/tests` pin, plus a group split only if sharding proves compile-bound).

## Files to touch

| File | New / change | What changes |
|---|---|---|
| `scripts/ci-shards.toml` | change | `[rust-test]` table: `"tools, wasm" = 1` becomes `"tools, wasm" = 4` (the line commented `"tools, wasm" = 1`). Nothing else in the file. |

Do not touch: anything under `.github/`, `bot/`, `.harness/`, `.squishy/` (person-only, see Open questions); no crate, app, `e2e/`, or `spec/` file. No spec section governs this change (CI sharding only), so no ruling note and no `proven_in` test are needed.

## Steps

1. In `scripts/ci-shards.toml`, in the `[rust-test]` table, change the line `"tools, wasm" = 1` to `"tools, wasm" = 4`. Copy the pattern from the `"server api" = 4` entry directly above it (same 4-shard precedent, set in #3585 for a 7m 24s job). 1104 s / 4 ≈ 276 s of test run per shard plus one shared compile, which the file's own guidance ("raise its count until each shard should finish under five") sizes for; 4 stays inside `matrix.py`'s `MAX_SHARDS = 8` and leaves room to raise further.
2. Verify the matrix locally with `python3 .github/ci/matrix.py matrix 2>&1 | grep "tools, wasm"`. Expect exactly four stderr lines: `rust (test tools, wasm 1/4)` through `rust (test tools, wasm 4/4)`, and no other group's job name changed. This works because `matrix.py` shards a group by CRC-32 of each test name, so every test lands in exactly one shard for any count and none is skipped or doubled.
3. Confirm the working tree holds only that file (`git status --porcelain` shows only `scripts/ci-shards.toml`) and stop. Do not edit `bot/tests/test_ci_matrix.py` to quiet its pin failure (bot/ is forbidden); the red pin is expected and the person updates it (Open questions).

## Tests

- Builder: `python3 .github/ci/matrix.py matrix` (read-only) showing the four `tools, wasm k/4` jobs, per step 2. No Rust or web test covers a TOML count change; do not run Workspace suites for this.
- Person, after the pin update: `python3 -m unittest bot.tests.test_ci_matrix -v` from the repo root, all green.
- Person, on the pull request's CI run: read each `rust (test tools, wasm k/4)` job's step times and confirm each is under 8 minutes (ci-duration.yml only files issues past 10, so the 8-minute check is manual).

## Done when

- [ ] `scripts/ci-shards.toml` holds `"tools, wasm" = 4` and nothing else changed.
- [ ] `matrix.py` lists exactly `tools, wasm 1/4`–`4/4` with all other jobs unchanged.
- [ ] No file outside `scripts/ci-shards.toml` is modified.
- [ ] The person has the exact pin diff and the conditional group split (Open questions).
- [ ] Each `tools, wasm k/4` job on the pull request finishes under 8 minutes, or the person has applied the group split instead.

## Risks

- A count splits the run, not the compile: each shard rebuilds the group's binaries (engine and cards as dependencies at opt-level 2, the tools binaries, run/shared/wasm). If the compile alone approaches 8 minutes, four shards still land over target; that outcome triggers the person's group split in Open questions rather than a higher count, since more shards would just repeat the compile on more runners.
- Until the person updates the pin, `bot selftest`'s `test_the_committed_files_give_todays_jobs` fails on the new job names. That failure is expected and named in Open questions; it must not be "fixed" from the bot side.
- No coverage is lost to sharding: hash sharding keeps every test in exactly one shard, and the closure has zero doc tests (every fenced block in `crates/tools`, `crates/run`, `crates/shared`, `crates/wasm` src is `text`, not `rust`) while the group already has no `doc` field.

## Open questions

- Person part 1 (blocks merge): update the pin in `bot/tests/test_ci_matrix.py`. In `JOBS`, replace the entry `"tools, wasm",` with `"tools, wasm 1/4", "tools, wasm 2/4", "tools, wasm 3/4", "tools, wasm 4/4",` (keeping its position after `"tools duos, selfplay",`). In `test_the_committed_files_give_todays_jobs`, change `jobs["tools, wasm"]["test"]` to `jobs["tools, wasm 1/4"]["test"]`. The shards-set assertion needs no change (`(1,4)`–`(4,4)` are already there from `server api`).
- Person part 2 (only if any `tools, wasm k/4` shard still runs 8 minutes or more): replace the `tools, wasm` block in `.github/ci/rust-test.toml` in place with these four groups, all keeping `scope = "tools_wasm"` and `cache = "tools-wasm"` so `scripts/ci-scope.sh` and the caches need no change, then update the pin's `JOBS` to the four new names:
  - `group = "tools unit"`, `test = "-p jackioh-tools --lib -- --skip fuzz:: --skip selfplay:: --skip positions::"`, `doc = "-p jackioh-tools"`
  - `group = "tools acceptance"`, `test = "-p jackioh-tools --test acceptance --test golden --test export_card_modes --test export_card_text --test perf"` (no `doc`; integration targets hold none, and the tools lib's is covered above)
  - `group = "run, shared"`, `test = "-p jackioh-run -p jackioh-shared"`, `doc = "-p jackioh-run -p jackioh-shared"`
  - `group = "wasm"`, `test = "-p jackioh-wasm -p jackioh-wasm-core -p jackioh-wasm-c"`, `doc = "-p jackioh-wasm -p jackioh-wasm-core -p jackioh-wasm-c"`
<!-- /jackioh-bot:plan -->
```

- A count splits the run, not the compile: each shard rebuilds the group's binaries (engine and cards as dependencies at opt-level 2, the tools binaries, run/shared/wasm). If the compile alone approaches 8 minutes, four shards still land over target; that outcome triggers the person's group split in Open questions rather than a higher count, since more shards would just repeat the compile on more runners.
- Until the person updates the pin, `bot selftest`'s `test_the_committed_files_give_todays_jobs` fails on the new job names. That failure is expected and named in Open questions; it must not be "fixed" from the bot side.
- No coverage is lost to sharding: hash sharding keeps every test in exactly one shard, and the closure has zero doc tests (every fenced block in `crates/tools`, `crates/run`, `crates/shared`, `crates/wasm` src is `text`, not `rust`) while the group already has no `doc` field.
